title: Affine Gaussian density integration
statement:
Let $I$ be a finite index set, let $c=(c_i)_{i\in I}\in\mathbb R^I$, let $s\in\mathbb R$ be nonzero, and let $f:\mathbb R^I\to\mathbb R$ be measurable. Then
\[
\int_{\mathbb R^I} f(c+sY)\,d\gamma_I(Y)=\int_{\mathbb R^I}\left(\prod_{i\in I} p_{c_i,s^2}(z_i)\right)f(z)\,dz,
\]
where $\gamma_I$ is the product of standard Gaussian measures, $dz$ is product Lebesgue measure, and $p_{m,v}$ is the Gaussian density with mean $m$ and variance $v$.
replaced: Let $I$ be finite, $c\in\mathbb R^I$, $s\ne0$, and $f:\mathbb R^I\to\mathbb R$ measurable. For a standard Gaussian vector $Y$, $\mathbb E f(c+sY)=\int_{\mathbb R^I}(\prod_i p_{s^2}(c_i,z_i))f(z)\,dz$, where $p_{s^2}$ is the scalar Gaussian density and nonintegrable integrals are assigned zero.
